prompt:
Design brief — your own take on this character. A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Platinum (백금) itself — the sovereign of the Platinum Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Age: early thirties — a poised, graceful face with soft contours; at most faint lines, no deep folds or under-eye bags.

You design her yourself: invent her face, eye colour, hairstyle, makeup, expression, pose and setting as a fresh, original take — do not follow any earlier design of this character. Her hair colour and costume are NOT free: take them from our designs below.

Style (fixed): A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish.

Inspiration only — her element: platinum: a dense, cool white metal that never changes — it does not rust, tarnish or dissolve in almost any acid; once tossed aside by Spanish gold-washers as worthless 'little silver', it became rarer and costlier than gold; for 130 years a small cylinder of platinum and iridium sealed under three nested glass bell jars was the kilogram itself, the measure of the world; a catalyst that makes hydrogen burst into flame and other substances transform at its touch while it stays untouched; aloof, exacting and incorruptible. Palette: cool satin platinum white, polished mirror silver, deep vault-black velvet, pale catalytic blue-white flame.

World (fixed): around 1889 at the Pavillon de Breteuil in Sèvres near Paris, the year the platinum-iridium prototype kilogram and metre were sanctioned: an underground vault where the kilogram is sealed beneath three nested glass bell jars, a hushed weighing room of precision balances in glass cases, and a cabinet of Döbereiner lamps that light themselves when hydrogen meets a sponge of platinum. Her costume and setting belong to this world.

Costume (choose one of ours, then add your own idea): pick ONE of these costume shapes from our set and keep its overall silhouette — 1) a fitted bodice and a long bustled ball gown sweeping out behind her, long gloves — an elegant, wide-trailing shape; 2) a long tailcoat over a waistcoat, a small silk top hat and a pocket-watch chain — a gentleman inventor's upright shape; 3) a double-breasted military greatcoat below the knee with brass buttons and epaulettes, tall boots — an angular, commanding shape; 4) a long leather coat with a bandolier of glass vials, brass goggles and long gloves — a mysterious experimenter's shape; 5) a clockwork gear rig worn on her back over a fitted vest, small brass fittings on arms and legs — the machinery makes the shape; 6) one large brass mechanical gauntlet covering a whole arm over an otherwise trim outfit — the contrast makes the shape; 7) an open crinoline cage of brass hoops below the waist under a sheer overskirt — a birdcage-wide shape. Then add one signature idea of your own drawn from her element, built into the construction of the outfit itself rather than as a print or a loose accessory — e.g. plates or cloth layered like crystals, scales or flames, a hem or sleeve cut into a shape from her element. Build it in this world's materials and our colours below.

Costume colours (ours): cool satin platinum white, polished mirror silver, deep vault-black velvet, pale catalytic blue-white flame.

Hair colour (fixed — ours): cool satin platinum-white hair with a soft untarnished sheen. Keep exactly this hair colour; only the hairstyle is yours.

Exposure (fixed): bold — her outfit shows skin by design (a deep neckline, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or short hem); intimate areas covered.

Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described above.

Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

If you have already drawn a free design of her in this session, make this one clearly different — another face and hairstyle (the same hair colour), another costume shape with another signature idea, another pose and setting.

Write your own detailed image prompt from this brief, then draw it. One figure only, natural hands with five fingers; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Pt) and atomic number (78) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.

My detailed design: choose the clockwork-device costume silhouette from the supplied set. A different adult metrology sovereign, softly sculpted heart-oval face, pale lavender-grey eyes, thoughtful serious expression, platinum-white hair in a short straight asymmetric bob tucked behind one ear, no crown. Her garment is a precisely fitted black velvet and ivory silk late Victorian technician ensemble with a low V neckline, bare shoulders, symmetrical silver shoulder straps and a short layered skirt over opaque fitted shorts, tall lace-up boots. Signature construction: a circular differential balance mechanism forms the back frame, with three concentric semicircular silver ribs and two small matched counterweights, completely integrated into her clothing rather than handheld; a miniature platinum-sponge lamp at her belt burns a pale blue-white flame. Both normal human arms and empty gloved hands clearly visible with five fingers. She stands full-body in the sunlit doorway to a historical instrument cabinet, one knee gently relaxed, body toward the viewer. Mechanical elements use fine Victorian silver and brass, no modern electronics, no armor plates, no corset. Distinct from the long ponytail tailcoat design; all fixed brief style, palette and framing retained.

generation.note: Original PNG is not committed; its sha256 is retained.
